Maria — thanks for sending these over and for the clear bullets. Quick response with our initial positions so we can converge quickly: 

1) Output ownership: We can accept a customer assignment for outputs derived solely from their input/data (i.e., product outputs they create) subject to the Order Form scope. We would like a brief carveout that allows Redwood to use de-identified, aggregated outputs for internal quality monitoring and safety (not model training).

2) Training on customer data: We understand the sensitivity. Redwood policy is to not train models on customer content unless there is an explicit opt-in. We can propose language that states Redwood will not use identifiable customer content for model training without a written opt-in, but we need the right to use aggregated telemetry (see feedback below) to maintain product safety and performance.

3) Feedback license: Rather than a blanket 2-year license, can we propose: a perpetual, worldwide, royalty-free license limited to non-personal, de-identified feedback and aggregated telemetry, explicitly excluding training on identifiable customer content. If Orbitron requires a term limit, propose a 5-year term with an auditability/escape ramp.

I'm attaching a short counter-redline with suggested phrasing and bracketed options where we need Orbitron input. Happy to hop on a 30-min call this week.

Thanks everyone for fast review and the clear asks. To keep procurement on schedule, here's a consolidated proposal and action items: 

Proposal (redlined language attached):
- Outputs: Orbitron retains title to outputs generated from Orbitron inputs. Redwood may use de-identified, aggregated outputs for safety, monitoring, and bug-fixing only; explicit prohibition on using such outputs for model training unless Orbitron provides a written opt-in.
- Feedback license: Redwood requests a perpetual, worldwide, royalty-free license limited strictly to non-personal, de-identified feedback and aggregated telemetry used for model quality and safety. As a compromise, if Orbitron insists on a term, Redwood will accept a 5-year term with a renewal option tied to the Order Form.
- De-identification: We propose a definition that cross-references NIST de-identification guidance (see attached language) and includes an operational audit protocol (annual, scoped to process controls, not content sampling).
- Commercial retraining limitation: Redwood agrees to a carveout that prevents using Orbitron-specific data to train standalone models that compete with Orbitron's product lines; standard product improvements and safety work remain permitted.
- IP handback/escrow: Offer an optional IP handback mechanism with a one-time transition fee and a documented reproducibility package; details in attached Order Form section.

Action items / timeline:
- Orbitron/Wilson: review attached redline and indicate whether the de-identification definition is acceptable — 48 hours.
- Redwood: prepare a short runbook and audit protocol (attached).
- If comments are minor, we propose a 30-min call Friday Apr 23 to resolve remaining brackets and finalize for procurement.

Attachments: rkim_proposed_counter_redline_v1.docx, runbook_deid_audit_protocol.pdf

Thanks — I appreciate the quick turnaround. If Orbitron needs to shorten the review window to meet Apr 26 procurement deadlines, let me know and we will prioritize.
